steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine oats, pastry flour, 1 cup brown sugar, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Mix in butter until crumbly. Press half of the mixture into the bottom of a 9-inch square baking pan.

Combine dates, water, and remaining 1/3 cup brown sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, and cook until thickened. Stir in lemon juice, and remove from heat. Spread the filling over the base, and spread the remaining crumb mixture on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is lightly toasted, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool before cutting into 12 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Gramma's Date Squares
raw_recipe.description: The best recipe for delicious date squares with buttery layers of goodness and a chewy oatmeal crust. The whole family will love this sweet treat.

review.reviewBody: 10 Star!!! I make these every day in my cafe for customers who can't get enough of them. Here are some tips to make them AMAZING! I like my squares to have a "crispy" texture rather than dry and loose, so I use a full 1 cup of BUTTER. I then melt it in the microwave until it is just past the really mushy stage. some will actually be melted completely. Remember, if your mix is dry in the bowl, it will be dry on your date squares! Mix the dry ingredients with the butter as instructed. However, after placing half the mixture in your pan, bake it for 15 minutes or until golden brown! This makes them easy to cut and they hold together much better than regular bars. No need to dice the dates, but do have a "squeeze" of each one quick to ensure there aren't any pits in them! Dates are sweet already. So if you just want to taste the dates, omit the brown sugar that is called for in the date mixture. Just add your water and lemon juice. Remove your pan from the oven and you can spread your dates over top right away. Crumble the rest of your mixture over top making sure your entire mixture is mixed with the butter really well. Bake until a golden brown. THESE FREEZE PERFECTLY! I wrap 6 in plastic wrap really well and use within a week so I'm not sure how long you can leave them in the freezer for. Lastly, DOUBLE THE RECIPE! Put it in a 9x13 or 10x14 pan and share with your friends. This is an awesome recipe!!! Thanks so much Michelle.

Wow, good recipe. I halved the sugar in the crust and put none in the filling (dates are so sweet anyway), used ½ c whole-wheat flour + ½ c all-purpose, and substituted ¼ c applesauce for some of the butter. Turned out beautiful, delicious (even better the next day) and almost guilt-free.

These are WONDERFUL!!!! It was like biting into my childhood....I grew up eating ethnic sweets and desserts filled w/dried fruits and nuts. So like others, I made changes too, but, I'm ADDING stars to this recipe review. I dont understand why people take stars away for a recipe they enjoyed but tweaked. TEN STARS here. These were my changes: I used 1/4 cup less brown sugar for the crust, added 1/2 cup chopped pecans, added 1/4 cup more oats (I used quick oats), and added cinnamon and nutmeg, a must! for the filling, do NOT chop dates, there is no need for that extra work. Simply take out the pits, place in a pan and gently warm w/water and 2 tbsp butter, that is key. No more sugar needed. Fold and stir to your preferred consistency, I like my dates soft and spreadable. I used a 9x13 glass pan, coated w/coconut oil, and baked the bottom crust first, 7 min. Then added the date layer and top crust and baked 20 min more. Powdered sugar makes these squares even prettier. I cannot wait to impress my parents. These cookies far exceeded my expectations and I'm so happy I read the reviews. Every baker and every oven is different, but these squares are perfect! Adding to my Christmas cookie list, thank you so much!!!!

This is my favorite date square recipe. Everybody loves them and I find them simple to make and delicious! This time I made them following the tips from lorrie ( most helpful positive review). All she suggested was Xtra butter and cook base 15 min before adding date mixture...OMG! What a difference, they were great before now thier amazing!!!! Thanks Michelle & lorrie

Great recipe to adjust to your own liking. As it is, there's waaay too much crumble (easily use half for 9") and I prefer adding pure vanilla extract instead of lemon. I also like a firmer base so I bake it for about 7 minutes before adding the filling and topping. Delicious!

I made it according to the recipe and they were awful. I think I know where the recipe and I went wrong.

Far too much sugar in the filling. Cut by half. Far too much flour in the crust. Cut by half. Half cup of sugar and add 1tsp of cinnamon.

Cream the butter and sugar before adding flour and oats.

3 cups of dates and extra water, used full cup of butter for the crumb mix and prebaked the bottom crust 18 minutes to get a nice firm base. This fits a larger pan than just a square baking dish. There's more crust/topping than you think!

Oh boy oh boy! Well, I bought a bag of dates thinking I liked dates (all the while, I was thinking of figs. I have a small child...brain no worky sometimes) - a big bag at costco. So, I came here and found this recipe to make for tomorrow's company. Delicious. My changes: 1. I doubled the butter; 2. I did not add brown sugar to the date mixture and 3. i baked the bottom layer for 15 minutes prior to adding the top two layers. So good - the butter flavor really comes through - the topping and bottom have a great consistency. I read some reviews where salt and baking soda were omitted - I would NOT omit the salt, you just need that little hit of salt and the texture of the mixture is very very good. I want to make this with apples and berries and all sorts of mixed fruits!
Delicious. I doubled and followed advice to bake first layer and omit sugar from date mixture. Sprinkled powdered sugar to serve which made them prettier.

A good basic recipe, but I added figs and a tablespoon of Molasses to the filling and I took Lorries advice and baked the bottom layer for 15 minutes. I also added extra butter and also cinnamon and crushed walnuts and hemp seeds to the crumbly mix. Vanilla and lemon juice was perfect in the filling.

Like many other users, I omitted the sugar from the date mixture, used only all-purpose flour, and pre-baked the bottom crust for 8 minutes. Absolutely amazing. Another tip: they MUST cool completely before you eat them. The flavors develop and they will not fall apart. 5 stars.
I added vanilla extract and marinated the chopped dates in some vanilla extract overnight too. Made them PERFECT, but I'm sure they are good without it too.

I wanted to try a different recipe than my tried and true from my grandmother. My recipe was always too moist I thought. Well this recipe was so dry. A lot of the topping was left in the pan after baking and getting the squares out. It did come out of the pan easily so that was a plus. Back to my tried and true! .

My husband’s favourite. I don’t add any brown sugar to the dates as we find them plenty sweet enough without. I use 1 cup butter and also pre bake the bottom for about 15 minutes as one other review suggested
Awesome recipe with no mess!

This is the perfect recipe! I only had 200grams of dates and that was fine. I cooked the dates for about 20 minutes because I prefer more of a purée than chunky pieces. I also added a dash of cinnamon to the filling. 10/10, will be saving this recipe, thank you!
It's great, just used all purpose flour, smells delightful!
I lost my gramma recipe but I found it a simpler one on this website. Take about bringing memories back..
First ever date squares, turned out great.
I made extra crumble and date mixture. So,I made a small square without the top layer. We actually liked it better… How long can we store the bars?
